title: Compare Titanic group rules on authorized competition data
summary: Actual-data verified for one recorded run: the same two group rules on five unchanged stratified folds of the official Titanic training file. The class-split change scored lower than the sex-only baseline (mean fold accuracy 0.7732 versus 0.7867).
split_definition: Five target-stratified folds with seed 17; each row validates once; group rules fit training rows only.
environment: Recorded with Python 3.12.13 and its standard library only on Darwin arm64, in one local CPU run on 2026-10-26. Other Python versions and platforms are not covered by this receipt. Set private input/output environment variables as documented before execution.
steps: Inspect the official data page and current rules, obtain authorized train.csv (and optional test.csv) yourself, and keep the files outside Git/public/dist.
Use the pinned four-file package and private environment variables; run both configurations on the same five seed-17 stratified folds.
Inspect per-fold differences, safe aggregated error slices and limitations; retain worse results, as the recorded run does.
Optionally run the notebook into a separate folder and compare fold results, aggregates, manifest and diagnostics exactly; validate any submission locally without publishing or uploading it.
limitations: One recorded run on one machine (Python 3.12.13, Darwin arm64, 2026-10-26); a notebook run of the same package matched it exactly but other environments are untested.
The class-split change underperformed: mean fold accuracy 0.7732 versus 0.7867 for the sex-only baseline, lower on three folds and tied on two.
Accuracy is the unweighted mean of five validation folds of train.csv, not a Kaggle leaderboard or hidden-test score, and no submission was made.
Random stratification does not isolate passenger families or tickets.
Traced Python allocations are not process RSS; no learner compute budget has been measured.
Input fingerprints show consistency with the recorded files, not dataset origin; access is the operator's recorded declaration.

project.outcome: Explain a controlled group-rule comparison using fixed train-only validation and aggregated diagnostics.
prerequisites: Run a local Python script and set private environment variables.
Explain a binary target, accuracy and a training/validation split.

access.instructions: Inspect https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/titanic/data and current rules yourself; obtain authorized train.csv and optional test.csv privately. Follow docs/titanic-actual-data-setup.md; no automatic acquisition or submission.
access.authorization: Recorded run used the official, unmodified train.csv and test.csv downloaded on 2026-10-26 through the Kaggle API by the repository owner's Kaggle account after accepting the competition rules. Readers must obtain their own copy: sign in, inspect and accept the current competition rules yourself, and download the official files; this site does not distribute them.

project.baseline: Fit sex-majority using training rows only on the fixed five stratified folds.
project.controlled_change: Compare sex-class-majority on exactly the same folds; retain worse outcomes.
diagnostics: Do the two methods agree in direction across all five unchanged folds?
Which sufficiently large sex/class slices have more errors, and what does the split omit?

troubleshooting.symptom: Missing authorized data or access failure
troubleshooting.recovery: Stop before running: inspect the official data page and rules, accept them yourself if eligible, and obtain your own copy. The recorded receipt does not grant access.
Use the setup recovery table, restore pinned files and rerun into a new private output directory; never publish raw errors or inputs.
